summary: A 1977 wooden live-in lookout beneath Napa Point above Swan Lake, Montana; a school-bus lookout stood on the site from 1969 to 1976.

access.note: Listed as available for emergencies and not regularly staffed; no public visiting or rental program found.

events.note: A school bus with an attached cupola served as the first permanent lookout, used through 1976.
Present 20-foot wooden live-in tower built to replace the school bus.
Forest Fire Lookout Association volunteers repaired the lookout and built a new staircase.
Two-year project wrapped up with a larger weighted trap door and new catwalk decking and handrails.
Registered as NHLR US 1493 (MT 71) on January 9, 2021.
Chapter assessment of whether the lookout could be stabilized to function safely on an intermittent basis.

corrections.why: NHLR and the 2025 chapter report both date the present 20-foot tower to 1977. The 1969 date marks the start of the school-bus lookout that the tower replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the lookout is not regularly staffed. The 2017 chapter report says DNRC staffs it part time. The record uses the 2017 report with its date and notes the register's view. Unresolved.
NHLR gives 4,409 ft (1,344 m), which matches the brief. firelookout.com and the 2025 chapter report give 4,448 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.

notes_for_editor: The 1977 build date is well supported and corrects the brief's 1969 build event. Staffing conflicts between NHLR (not regularly staffed) and the 2017 chapter report (DNRC part time); the as-of date is 2017. Current access is unconfirmed; no visiting or rental program found. height_m 6.1 converts the reported 20 feet of cab height, which is an inference from two sources. The 2016 Whitefish article calls Little Napa an L-4 design lookout in passing; design was not recorded because no source states it directly. One WebSearch was used. Five page reads.
